gap: No result ChatGPT got states Netflix's own rule: casting Netflix from a phone or tablet only works to a 3rd-gen-or-older Chromecast, a Google Nest Hub, or select cast-enabled Vizio and Compal TVs, and casting or mirroring needs a Standard or Premium plan. So a Wi-Fi mini projector without a licensed Netflix app built in, such as the Aurzen ZIP, cannot show Netflix wirelessly at all.
standout_why: I checked three cited pages. The iTechGuides MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 page says both have 'licensed Netflix' but never says why that matters or that phone casting and mirroring of Netflix is blocked. The RTINGS and TechRadar pages came back without their article text, and neither showed any Netflix, mirroring or DRM content. Of the uncited results, kiddofspeed says only 'Screen mirroring also has copy-protection issues with some apps, particularly Netflix', and misec says 'HDCP restrictions mean Netflix, Prime Video, and Hulu cannot mirror directly from your phone' for one budget pick. Neither names Netflix's own device list or plan rule, and neither tells shoppers to make a licensed built-in app a must-have. So rivals have part of the point, and the source-backed rule is new.
decides: It confirms that the Google TV and licensed-Netflix picks (XGIMI MoGo 4, MoGo 2 Pro, Aurzen EAZZE D1 and D1 air) are the safe answer for a shopper who wants Netflix. It also rules out mirroring-only Wi-Fi mini projectors like the Aurzen ZIP for Netflix, Hulu and Disney+ unless an extra dongle is bought. On a Wi-Fi projector, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth alone are not enough; the licensed app is the feature that decides it.

findings.label: Netflix phone-to-TV casting: supported devices
findings.value: Only Chromecast 3rd gen or older (no physical remote), Google Nest Hub Smart Display, select cast-enabled Vizio TVs and select cast-enabled Compal TVs. Otherwise 'you won't be able to cast Netflix to your TV from your phone or tablet.'
findings.source_title: Cast device or cast icon isn't showing in the Netflix app | Netflix Help Center
findings.note: Netflix's own help page. No projector is on the list, so a projector's built-in casting or mirroring receiver is not a supported Netflix target.

findings.label: Netflix plans that allow casting or mirroring
findings.value: Standard or Premium only ('Casting or mirroring is available on Standard or Premium plans')
findings.source_title: Cast device or cast icon isn't showing in the Netflix app | Netflix Help Center
findings.note: Shoppers on the ad-supported plan cannot cast or mirror Netflix, even to devices that are supported.

findings.label: Why Netflix fails on projectors (maker's explanation)
findings.value: 'Netflix uses HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) technology'; 'If your projector or HDMI cable does not support HDCP, it will not be able to stream Netflix'; iPhone casting failures 'may be due to Digital Rights Management (DRM) restrictions that prevent certain content from being mirrored or cast.'
findings.source_title: Why Can't I Play Netflix on My Projector? Troubleshooting Tips and Fixes – Nebula-US (dated 2025-01-23)
findings.note: Projector maker (Anker Nebula) explains the copy-protection mechanism.

findings.label: Symptom when mirroring Netflix to a projector
findings.value: 'The screen mirroring function is not supported and may result in a black screen with audio due to limitations with Netflix.'
findings.source_title: How do I watch Netflix on the M1 or M1+ with my mobile phone? (ViewSonic support)
findings.note: Maker support article for the ViewSonic M1 and M1+ mini projectors. It describes Android screen mirroring.
